notes: Hand-assembled, not generated by `tubuild.py create`: tu_map cannot segment arm9/main, so there was no candidate id to create from. The schema follows the arm9/dCc_c and arm9/Clipper entries, which took the same route.

dCcAc_c is the cylinder collision primitive attached to an dActor_c: Init fixes radius/height/flags on the dCc_c base and stores the owner back-pointer; both virtuals read through owner (GetPos returns the owner's dActor_c+0x5c position, GetOwnerID returns owner->uniqueID at +4).

dCcAcPos_c, the derived class adding Vector3 pos at +0x34, is this TU through its lifecycle. SetPosRelativeToActor and Init open the run at 0x0201489c/0x020148c8. Both Init methods are native out-of-line members taking the scalar Fix12i (mangled `i`), byte-identical to the former C-linkage definitions.

LIFECYCLE TAIL: D0 0x02014a34, D1 0x02014a60 and C1 0x02014a84 are the same ~dCcAcPos_c() and dCcAcPos_c() that emit D2 and C2. Those two have no ROM home and are deadstripped. Under default deferred codegen the kept order is D0, D1, C1, above GetPos. _ZTV10dCcAcPos_c, _ZTI10dCcAcPos_c and _ZTS10dCcAcPos_c externalize as deadstrip-data. Slot 3 stays the veneer: dCcAcPos_c::GetOwnerID is the qualified tail-call, which -interworking lowers to the 12-byte sequence at 0x02014a20, and the emitted vtable relocates the slot to that symbol. An inherited slot would relocate to _ZN7dCcAc_c10GetOwnerIDEv (0x0201493c) and the deadstrip-data compare would fail. The old address name func_02014a20 was that veneer.

The whole class folds, lifecycle variants included: the cartridge's D2,D0,D1,C1,C2 order for dCcAc_c is the order one ~dCcAc_c() plus one dCcAc_c() emits under deferred codegen, and dCcAcPos_c's kept D0,D1,C1 follow the same way once D2 and C2 are dropped. The run is written ROM-descending because mwccarm emits .text in reverse source order, so the emitted object carries the functions ascending 0x0201489c..0x02014aa8.
